metadata.description: Source code for the manuscript "Unsupervised Abnormal Behavior Recognition System for Older Adults Living Alone Using DBSCAN and Expert Rules". The repository includes the implementation of the proposed anomaly detection algorithm. Additionally, the extracted feature files for each CASAS dataset are provided. These feature datasets were generated by processing the original publicly available datasets from the CASAS Smart Home Project and are included to facilitate reproducibility of the reported experiments.

metadata.title: Unsupervised Machine Learning for Risk-Based Integrity Assessment of Underground Steel Pipelines: Bulk Water Distribution Utilities
metadata.description:
ABSTRACT:

Aging big-diameter underground steel pipelines pose significant sustainability and operational challenges for bulk water distribution utilities. These challenges include, but are not limited to, an increased risk of underground big-diameter pipeline failure and rising costs for asset condition assessments. We developed and tested a unsupervised machine-learning framework to improve pipeline condition assessment, predictive maintenance, and inspection prioritisation using real-world secondary data. We combined mixed-data clustering, non-linear dimensionality reduction, anomaly detection, and association rule mining to identify complex patterns in the condition of underground steel pipelines without excavation. Our results indicate that mixed-type clustering methods produce stable, well-separated condition groups and outperform numeric-only methods. Non-linear embeddings show clear separability, and anomaly detection reliably pinpoints high-risk pipeline segments. Association rules reveal hidden connections between pipeline attributes, enhancing clarity and engineering relevance. This framework enables data-driven decision-making, reduces unplanned maintenance, and supports efficient resource use by extending the lifespans of large-diameter underground pipeline assets and boosting operational reliability. This study supports sustainable asset management and improved operations in bulk water distribution pipeline systems through practical, scalable unsupervised analytics.

Keywords: Unsupervised Machine Learning, Big-diameter steel pipeline, Water Utilities.

metadata.title: When QSAR Fails: Dataset Bias, SAR Fragmentation, and the Instability of Analog-Series Benchmarks in HIV-1 Integrase Modeling
metadata.description:
This is version 2.0 of the deposit supporting the manuscript "When QSAR Fails: Dataset Bias, SAR Fragmentation, and the Instability of Analog-Series Benchmarks in HIV-1 Integrase Modeling," prepared during major revision at Molecular Informatics. Version 1.0 remains archived unchanged for provenance.

Version 2.0 corrects and extends the original analysis in response to peer review. Preprocessing is now leakage-free, with imputation, missing-column filtering, and zero-variance removal fitted on the training fold only. The eps-sensitivity analysis is replaced by a repeated grouped-split reanalysis of 30 seeds per threshold, which supersedes the original single-seed results; the previously reported three-regime interpretation is withdrawn in favour of a demonstrated relationship between dominant-cluster fraction and benchmark instability. A second, externally curated target (thrombin, CHEMBL204, from the MoleculeACE benchmark) confirms the effect generalises and is governed by cluster-size concentration rather than target identity. Bootstrap confidence intervals, a negative-analog-bias stratification with UMAP projection, a hyperparameter-tuning robustness check, an AUC permutation test, and a heteroscedasticity-aware noise-ceiling analysis with an archived replicate-level table are added.

Contents: a leakage-corrected, deterministic pipeline as a Python package; numbered analysis scripts for every check; results tables and figures; the curated dataset and replicate-level variance table; and a CHANGELOG mapping each change to the reviewer comment that prompted it. Third-party benchmark data from MoleculeACE (ChEMBL-derived, CC BY-SA) is not redistributed here; a pointer and fetch instructions are provided so the second-target analysis remains fully reproducible.

metadata.title: Machine learning-driven insights into social media's influence on student mental health and academic stress: research trends, challenges, and future directions
metadata.description: Social media's growing pervasiveness in students' daily life has raised serious concerns about psychological health in addition to providing previously unheard-of chances for interaction. Social media's introduction has had a profound impact on how students communicate, learn, and view academic difficulties. Although these platforms make it easier to communicate, collaborate, and share material, they also come with concerns including information overload, social comparison, and distraction, all of which can lead to academic stress. The relationship between social media use and student mental health is examined in this survey paper, which highlights the ways in which different methods are being applied to assess, forecast, and potentially lessen psychological distress in academic populations. The study investigates how data-driven approaches and Machine Learning (ML) could be used to spot stressful trends in online behavior. We have highlighted research gaps and offer future options for creating successful interventions and frameworks for digital well-being by examining recent literature. Additionally, this study summarizes previous research on machine learning models intended to identify, forecast, and comprehend mental health issues in students based on their interactions on social media.

metadata.title: DBSCAN ДЛЯ КЛАСТЕРИЗАЦІЇ АСТРОФІЗИЧНИХ ОБ'ЄКТІВ
metadata.description:
Запропоновано алгоритм DBSCAN та комплексне оцінювання кластеризації як за наявності, так і за відсутності міток. 

Для реалізації задачі використано еталонний набір даних — 'Star Type Classification / NASA'  https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/brsdincer/star-type-classification

Застосовувати для подальших астрономічних досліджень та класифікації космічних об'єктів: автоматичне групування нових відкритих астрономічних об'єктів за спектральними та фізичними характеристиками; виявлення аномальних космічних тіл (зокрема, за допомогою властивості DBSCAN виділяти шумові точки, які не підпадають під жоден кластер). Подальші можливості: запускати нові алгоритми на цьому ж датасеті та використовувати отримані результати, як порівняльний орієнтир для валідації мабутніх моделей.

metadata.title: Source Code for Static (K-Means, DBSCAN) and Dynamic (DTW) Clustering Algorithms
metadata.description:
This repository contains the source code for a hybrid customer segmentation framework combining static RFM (Recency, Frequency, Monetary) analysis and dynamic time-series behavioral clustering. 

The project segments customers based on their transactional value patterns and evaluates their purchasing trends over time using static methods (K-Means & DBSCAN) and a dynamic temporal method (TimeSeriesKMeans with Dynamic Time Warping).

Data Pipeline & Methodology:

  1. RFM Feature Engineering: Transactional data is aggregated per customer based on a specific snapshot cutoff (October 31, 2025) to compute Recency, Frequency, and Monetary metrics.
  2. Data Preprocessing: Features are scaled using standard normalization (`StandardScaler`) to balance feature variances.
  3. Static Clustering (RFM Space):
    • K-Means Clustering: Optimized using the Elbow Method to partition customers into static value tiers (k=4).
    • DBSCAN: Used as a density-based baseline to detect spatial structures and transactional outliers (noise).
    • Validation: Performance is evaluated using the Silhouette Score, confirming K-Means dominance for this specific dataset geometry.
  4. Dynamic Clustering (Temporal Space):
    • Weekly transactional time-series data is constructed for each customer.
    • TimeSeriesKMeans with Dynamic Time Warping (DTW): Used to capture non-linear, time-shifted transactional behaviors and group customers based on their dynamic spending trajectories.
    • Validation: Evaluated using a precomputed DTW distance matrix to calculate the temporal Silhouette Score.
  5. Hybrid Integration: The static and dynamic cluster assignments are combined to generate a multi-dimensional customer profile matrix.

Repository Structure

  1. `clustering.py`: The main Python script containing data loading, RFM calculations, modeling, visualization, and validation pipelines.
  2. `data_valid.csv`: Raw input dataset containing customer transaction histories.
  3. `clustering_result.csv`: Output file mapping `CustomerID` to both its `Static_Kmeans_Cluster` and `TS_Cluster` labels.

Prerequisites & Dependencies
To replicate this pipeline, install the required packages via pip:
pip install pandas numpy scikit-learn tslearn scipy matplotlib seaborn

metadata.title: AI-Driven Smart Citizen Complaint Platform  using Arabic NLP and Clustering
metadata.description:
The Smart Citizen Complaint Platform is an AI-driven complaint management system designed 
to enhance the efficiency of collecting, analyzing, prioritizing, and routing citizen complaints. 
The platform integrates Arabic Natural Language Processing (NLP), complaint clustering, and 
multi-factor reliability scoring to reduce manual workload and support faster and more accurate 
decision-making in public service environments. 
The system accepts complaint text along with metadata such as category, area, date, and location. 
After secure OTP-based user verification, the platform applies transformer-based Arabic NLP 
models to automatically classify complaints and estimate their urgency 
The system architecture is role-based, involving citizens, employees, and administrators. Citizens 
can submit and track complaints, employees handle and update complaint status, and 
administrators monitor reports, system statistics, and operational performance through dynamic 
dashboards and interactive heat maps. 
An experimental evaluation was conducted using Arabic complaint datasets to assess the 
performance of transformer-based models. The results showed that AraBERT achieved the best 
performance with an accuracy of 0.9167 and an F1-score of 0.9167, outperforming MARBERT 
(accuracy 0.910, F1-score 0.909). The experiments also revealed that minimal preprocessing 
combined with AraBERTPreprocessor provides the most effective setup, while aggressive 
preprocessing techniques negatively impact performance due to loss of contextual information.

 

This work was conducted at Arab International University (AIU), Syria. The official website of the university is: https://www.aiu.edu.sy
